title: Fire Extinguishers
description: Arm yourself with the right extinguisher for each fire. Master fire-fighting tools to seize ember 5.

content.value: For fires involving wood, paper and cloth, WATER is the best and cheapest extinguisher. It cools the fuel and cuts off oxygen with steam. But as we learned, water is wrong for oil and electrical fires.

CARBON DIOXIDE (CO₂) is an excellent fire extinguisher, especially for electrical and oil fires. Being heavier than air, CO₂ covers the fire like a blanket and cuts off the oxygen supply. It also cools the fuel. Best of all, it does not damage electrical equipment and leaves no mess.

EXTINGUISHER  BEST FOR                HOW IT WORKS
💧  Water       wood, paper, cloth      cools + cuts oxygen
🧯  CO₂         electrical, oil fires   blankets out oxygen + cools
🏖️  Sand/foam   small oil fires         cuts off oxygen

Some extinguishers release CO₂ from a cylinder; others produce it from chemicals like bicarbonates. However it's made, the CO₂ smothers the flames by forming a heavy layer that keeps oxygen away — breaking the fire triangle.
CO₂ is the go-to for electrical fires because it doesn't conduct electricity and leaves no residue on delicate equipment. Water on an electrical fire could give a deadly shock.
Key Takeaway: Water extinguishes wood/paper/cloth fires by cooling. Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is best for electrical and oil fires — it blankets the fire, cutting off oxygen without damaging equipment.

quiz.question: Why is carbon dioxide good for putting out electrical fires?
options: It cuts off oxygen without damaging equipment or giving shocks
It adds fuel to the fire
quiz.explain: CO₂ smothers the fire and does not conduct electricity, so it's safe on electrical fires.

quiz.question: Carbon dioxide can blanket a fire because it is…
quiz.explain: Being heavier than air, CO₂ settles over the fire and cuts off the oxygen supply.

quiz.question: The best cheap extinguisher for a burning pile of paper is…
quiz.explain: Water cools and smothers wood, paper and cloth fires effectively.
